html:
In January 2002 Mount Nyiragongo, a volcano in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, erupted and sent rivers of lava through the city of Goma on the north shore of Lake Kivu.

Nyiragongo stands in the Virunga Mountains, on the edge of the East African Rift. Its crater holds one of the world's few long-lived lava lakes. Its lava is unusually runny and can flow very fast; an eruption in 1977 had already killed many people.

In 2002 cracks opened on the volcano's flanks and lava poured downhill into Goma. It covered part of the city centre and the airport runway and destroyed thousands of homes. Hundreds of thousands of people fled, many across the border into Gisenyi in Rwanda. More than a hundred died, many in a fuel station explosion.

The eruption hit a region already wrecked by the Second Congo War, with Goma in rebel hands. Most people returned and rebuilt on the cooled lava. Nyiragongo erupted again in 2021.
sum: In January 2002 Mount Nyiragongo, a volcano in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, erupted and sent rivers of lava through the city of Goma on the north shore of Lake Kivu.
